::: {.why}
The data is free, complete and point-in-time by construction, and the reason few people use it is that the schema is genuinely awkward, which is a one-day problem rather than a permanent one.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Load a quarter of the financial statement data sets and extract one tag for the full universe with the filing date attached.
- Say what the ADSH identifier is and why it is what makes the data point-in-time.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Build the loader in qlib/ingest_fundamentals.py: parse the submission and numeric files, join on the accession identifier, and produce a long table of company, tag, fiscal period, value, filing date. Write it into the store with the three-date schema from day 137.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Extract one usable series end to end: total assets or shareholders equity for your universe, quarterly, with filing dates, over five years. Check a handful of values against the company's actual filing to confirm you have the right tag and the right sign.
:::
:::

## The running strategy

::: {.project}
Fundamental data now comes from EDGAR directly into the store with filing dates attached, so every fundamental signal in the book is point-in-time by construction rather than by a lag applied afterwards.
:::
